source.extractionNote: Single run over all 8 variants (Kind × Shape); metadata frame 8190:179 read the same day it was authored.

summary: A full-size preview over the page, opened from the item being viewed. Images, videos and PDFs render themselves; anything else shows a drawn file sheet with the file's glyph and “No preview for this file”. A toolbar names the item and offers open in a new tab, download and close; previous, next and the arrow keys page through the list. Backdrop, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock come from Dialog; everything visual comes from the token layer.

intent.image: Never set by hand — derived from the item’s MIME type or extension. An image renders itself, capped at 70% of the viewport’s height, keeping its own ratio.
intent.video: Fills the stage’s width where it can; the height cap contains it and the picture keeps its own ratio inside the player.
intent.pdf: An embedded document at 70% of the viewport’s height.
intent.other: No preview. A drawn file sheet carries the file’s glyph and “No preview for this file”.

intent.rounded: The default, matching the system’s other rounded controls. Shape also picks the glyph family for every icon in the toolbar and navigation.
intent.sharp: Square corners on the panel and stage, with the sharp glyph family.

intent.true: The toolbar offers open in a new tab. The action disables itself when the item has no URL rather than failing silently.
intent.false: Removes the action from the toolbar.

intent.true: The toolbar offers download, named after the item. It disables itself when the item has no URL.
intent.false: Removes the action from the toolbar.

intent.true: Previous and next float at the stage’s sides and the arrow keys page too. With a single item, navigation hides itself whatever this is set to.
intent.false: Hides paging even when several items are passed.

name.intent: The item’s name in the toolbar, from its name, its file’s name or its URL; “Untitled” when none exists.

counter.intent: “{index} of {count}”, shown only while paging through several items.

intent.true: Paging slides and the stage’s height follows — see Behavior & Motion Intent. Always yields to the reduced-motion preference. A code property; the variants don’t model it.
intent.false: Paging and the height change land instantly, with nothing in between.

contentInputs.note: The drawn media in the variants is a placeholder — the library ships no images. In code the real file renders.

anatomy.role: The raised surface over the backdrop: surface/overlay with a border/default stroke and Dialog’s shadow/large on shadow/soft. Width defaults to control/lg × 16, never wider than the viewport less space/page each side.

paint.effects: Shadow/large (shadow/large/x·y·blur on shadow/soft, plus shadow/small/x·y·blur on shadow/hard)

anatomy.role: Names the item, counts the pages and holds open in new, download and close — each behind its own property, every one an Icon Button.
The item’s name; fills the row and truncates at one line.
“{index} of {count}” between the name and the actions.
The media well: surface/shade dims the panel behind the content, minimum height control/lg × 6. The track of frames slides inside it, clipped.

layout.padding: space/lg top and bottom for image, space/none otherwise

paint.fill: surface/subtle (see issues — metadata and code say surface/shade)

anatomy.role: The current item’s rendering (image and video kinds). Image sits on surface/card; video on surface/inverse, filling the stage’s width.
The embedded document (pdf kind), filling the stage’s width on surface/card with Shadow/medium.
The file sheet for the other kind: a portrait card with a folded corner, the file’s glyph centred, and “No preview for this file” below.

layout.padding: space/3xl top and bottom, space/xl sides

paint.radius: radius/element-md, with the top-right corner radius/none under the fold

stroke.width: stroke/thin on the bottom and left sides only

variants._note: Root and stage heights are measured observations of the placeholder media, not design values — in code the stage follows the real frame.

table.stage.fill-child: unpreviewable sheet + “No preview for this file”

secondaryAxis.effect: sharp swaps every radius to radius/none (root, stage, sheet, fold) and switches every nested Icon Button and glyph to the sharp family; nothing else changes.

subcomponents.name: Icon Button
subcomponents.note: Own spec; Lightbox pins Size=medium and uses Flavour=subtle in the toolbar, Flavour=contrast for navigation, Shape following shape.

subcomponents.name: Icon
subcomponents.note: Size=large placeholder glyphs inside the drawn media; in code the real file renders and the sheet glyph comes from the file’s kind.

icons.note: image and document appear only as placeholder art inside the drawn media/sheet. Icon colour is currentColor and size is the nested Icon’s own variant (large in the sheet, Icon Button’s own inside buttons); the rounded/sharp axis is a font-family swap pinned by shape.

states.trigger: Index set on a closed lightbox
states.whatChanges: Backdrop and panel appear with the current frame already in place. Transitions arm one frame after opening, so the first frame never slides in.

states.trigger: Previous / next, or the arrow keys
states.whatChanges: The track slides to the new frame — the old one glides out as the new one glides in — and the stage’s height follows on the same timing. An interrupted page glides on to the new target instead of restarting.

states.trigger: The current item’s media reports real dimensions
states.whatChanges: The stage re-measures the frame and eases to its true height. Media sizes arrive after mount, so the first measure is never final.
The whole motion block turns off: paging and height changes land instantly, whatever Animated says.
The dialog unmounts; offscreen videos are already paused, and the open-in-place reset arms for the next open.

behavior.description: Paging is one transition on the track’s slide and one on the stage’s height: 400ms on cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1), slower than the small controls’ 250ms because the frames are large and travel far — the slide reads as a scene change, not a flick. Transitions, not keyed animations: an interrupted page glides to the new target instead of restarting, and nothing remounts. No motion token exists yet; the timing is a literal, as Message Input and Switch.
The first shown frame appears in place. Transitions switch on one frame after the lightbox opens, so only real paging slides — without this gate the opening frame slides in from the side.

The stage’s height follows the current frame on the paging timing, as a measured length. Both ends of a height transition must be real lengths — auto never interpolates — so the height is always written as a value, never left to the content.

An image or video only knows its real size once it loads, and a PDF’s load event is unreliable. The stage re-measures when media gains dimensions and again when the panel mounts; never trust the first measure.

The track is pinned to the stage, never sized by its content. Sized by content, the tallest frame (a 70vh document) inflates it past the stage, it overflows, and every frame centres against the oversized box instead of the visible window.

Media caps at 70% of the viewport’s height and keeps its own ratio. Video fills the stage’s width where it can; the cap contains it. The panel never grows wider than the viewport less space/page each side, nor taller than it less the same.
A frame slid out of view pauses its video. Neighbouring frames stay mounted so paging never reloads — which also means they keep playing unless paused.
Animated always yields to the reduced-motion preference: the motion block turns off entirely rather than shortening.

content.description: The item’s name in the toolbar, from its name, its file’s name or its URL; “Untitled” when none exists.
“{index} of {count}”, shown only while paging through several items.
The list being previewed. Neighbouring items stay mounted either side of the current one, so paging never reloads media or flickers.
The drawn media in the variants is a placeholder — the library ships no images. In code the real file renders.

do: Open the lightbox from the thing being previewed — a thumbnail, an attachment row — and return focus there when it closes.
Pass every related item in one list, so previous, next and the arrow keys page through the whole set without reopening.
dont: Don’t page by swapping frames. The track slides what is already mounted; remounting reloads media and flickers.
Don’t fix the stage’s height or leave it auto. It follows the current frame as a measured value — auto cannot animate, and a fixed height crops tall media.

accessibility: Backdrop, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock come from Dialog, so focus cannot leave the panel while it is open.
Previous and next are labelled buttons and the arrow keys page as well; with one item, navigation disappears entirely.
Open in new and download disable themselves when the item has no URL rather than failing silently.
Reduced motion turns all sliding off; nothing is communicated by motion alone.
The file sheet names the file and says “No preview for this file”, so an unpreviewable item is still announced.
A frame slid out of view pauses its video, so sound never continues behind another frame.

layoutTheming.description: control/lg × 16 by default (--zds-lightbox-width in code), capped at the viewport less space/page each side.
Fits its content up to the viewport less space/page top and bottom; the stage follows the current frame.
control/lg × 6 minimum; surface/shade fill; radius/element-sm, radius/none when sharp.
Up to 70% of the viewport’s height, keeping its ratio; shadow/medium on shadow/soft — the panel itself carries shadow/large.
space/md around the panel, space/sm between toolbar and stage.
radius/element-md on the panel, radius/element-sm on the stage; radius/none everywhere when sharp.
stroke/thin on border/default around the panel.
surface/overlay panel, surface/shade stage, foreground/primary text. Every value is a semantic token; nothing hardcodes a colour, so modes and extensions arrive free.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: The stage’s fill is bound to surface/subtle in every Figma variant, but the metadata’s Layout & Theming row and the implementation both say surface/shade (the translucent elevate fill). One of the two is wrong; the intended value is surface/shade so content dims what is behind it.

The stage’s minimum height is a raw measurement (288Px, matching control/lg × 6 as the metadata states) with no variable bound — Figma has no way to bind min-height to control/lg × 16-style arithmetic. Implement it as calc on control/lg, not as a literal.
Motion timing (400ms, cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1)) is a literal: the token export has no motion collection. The metadata says so; the same literal convention is used by Message Input and Switch.
animated exists only in code; the variants don’t model it. kind is derived from the item’s MIME type or extension, never set by a consumer — both are stated in the metadata.

stage paddingTop/Bottom (space/lg) is bound only in the image variants — the other kinds remove the padding so media fills the stage; intended, per the variant table. The fold’s bottomLeftRadius binding (radius/element-sm) exists only in rounded; sharp removes every radius.
The sheet fold’s per-side stroke weights read as a raw [0,0,1,1] composite, but the two drawn sides (bottom, left) are each bound to stroke/thin; the zero sides are by design.

From the set description, verbatim: the media are placeholders (no images in the library); the backdrop (overlay/scrim), portal, focus trap and Escape come from Dialog in code; the paging slide (400ms, no motion token) isn’t drawn. The sheet’s fold uses surface/subtle because surface/sunken has no variable.

The counter’s visibility is tied to Show Navigation in Figma; the metadata’s Content row says it shows “only while paging through several items” — in code that is the same condition, since navigation hides itself with one item.
The root width (768Px) is fixed in Figma and equals control/lg × 16, the stated default; per-kind root heights in the variant table are placeholder-media measurements, not design values.
